gap: No result ChatGPT got states that The Gadgeteer found the TESmart HDC202-X24 Thunderbolt KVM tops out at 60 fps at 3440×1440 on an ultrawide, that Ubergizmo saw the Sabrent USB-CKDH take 3–7 seconds to switch, or that igor'sLAB ran the Level1Techs DP 1.4 dual-monitor KVM at 1440p 144 Hz with G-Sync working and no added input lag.
standout_why: I opened both pages ChatGPT cited and two top uncited results. Racks & Watts (updated 2026-11-01) lists only maker specs for StarTech SV231HU34K6/SV231DPDDUA2/SV431HU34K6 and AV Access iDock C10. It gives no switch time, latency or tested charging figure and names no tester. TESmart's 2026 buying guide gives only spec claims (HDC203-PM24 100 W PD, HDK202-M24 dual 4K144) and says 'tested across real-world workflows' with no results. The Office Journal (laptop + desktop) gives only listing specs and tells readers to 'verify power delivery wattage' themselves. DeskDNA likewise has no measurements. None of these pages names a reviewer, a figure and a date, so a side-by-side of named hands-on findings would be new. It is thin, though: no lab has published a stopwatch or USB-meter number for the main candidates.
decides: This confirms the picks more than it changes them. For a gamer with an ultrawide, the HDC202-X24 should be shown as 60 Hz at 3440×1440 (The Gadgeteer), so the Level1Techs DP 1.4 unit is the only candidate with a named high-refresh run on record (igor'sLAB: 1440p 144 Hz with G-Sync, no added input lag). It needs a dock for the laptop and has no EDID emulation. The Sabrent USB-CKDH's 3–7 s switch (Ubergizmo) adds to its desktop-needs-USB-C-video drawback, so it should stay at the bottom. For the iDock M10, Macworld's 2026 review backs 'Yes' for two screens on Pro/Max and adds that base M3 needs the lid closed and that the spare USB-C port gives only 7.5 W.

findings.label: Refresh reached at ultrawide native resolution through the KVM (hands-on)
findings.source_title: TESmart thunderbolt KVM switch review – great as long as you're fine with 4k60FPS or 2K screens (The Gadgeteer, Matt Gregersen, 2025-06-04)
findings.note: Quote: 'the KVM switch tops out at 60 FPS at native resolution (3440 x 1440 pixels)'. The reviewer puts this down to bandwidth. The monitor was an INNOCN 34Q1R OLED ultrawide, with a Thunderbolt gaming laptop on PC-1 and a mini-PC on PC-2. This is an observation, not an instrument measurement. 3440×1440 is 4.95 MP against 3.69 MP for 2560×1440, so it does not disprove a 2560×1440@120 spec. Our table's '1440p@120' should say it means 16:9. The sample was supplied free by TESmart. The review also reports 'fast switching' with no figure.

findings.label: Switch time, all devices and monitors (hands-on)
findings.source_title: Sabrent USB Type-C Dual KVM Switch review (Ubergizmo, Hubert Nguyen, 2023-05-07)
findings.note: Quote: 'it takes 3-7 seconds for all the devices and monitors to come over.' The review gives no stopwatch method. The reviewer did not test power delivery ('I didn't use the power-delivery feature') and notes the shared ports are USB 2.0.

findings.product: Level1Techs DP 1.4 KVM dual monitor / 2 computers
findings.label: Modes run in use; adaptive sync; input lag (hands-on)
findings.value: 1440p 144 Hz and 2160p 60 Hz ran with no problems; G-Sync/adaptive sync worked, no added input lag
findings.source_title: 2 PCs, 1 Desk, 0 Chaos – Level1Techs DisplayPort 1.4 Dual-Monitor KVM Switch | Usability Test (igor'sLAB, Xaver Amberger, 2021-03-02)
findings.note: Quotes: 'I had no problems whatsoever with running 1440p 144Hz and 2160p 60 Hz monitors' and 'G-Sync or adaptive sync work just fine and there is no additional input lag.' The input-lag claim is the reviewer's judgement; no lag number is given. 4K120 is not a tested result. The test is from 2021 on the same product line. A wireless dongle on a USB 2.0 HID port dropped to half sensitivity at times, which moving it to a USB 3.0 port fixed.

findings.label: Two extended displays by Mac chip (review)
findings.value: M1/M2 Pro/Max or later: two displays; base M3: two displays only with the lid closed; base M1/M2 and MacBook Neo: one external display
findings.source_title: AV Access iDock M10 Review: The Best KVM Dock for MacBook and PC Setups? (Macworld, Simon Jary, 2026-06-02)
findings.note: Quotes: 'Two monitors are supported on base M3 MacBooks' … 'the laptop's lid must remain closed'. Switching is described only as 'near-instant', with no seconds figure. The review uses two Thunderbolt ports on the MacBook. Price at review: $289.99 at Amazon/AV Access, $255 at Walmart.

findings.label: Charging from the spare USB-C port (review, stated not metered)
findings.source_title: AV Access iDock M10 Review (Macworld, Simon Jary, 2026-06-02)
findings.note: Quote: 'The one spare USB-C port can output at 7.5W, which will charge an iPhone or iPad but slowly'. Macworld lists weak USB charging as a con. These are stated specs, not USB-meter readings. Power supply: 120 W.
